key_facts: A House China Committee probe found China Telecom, China Mobile, and China Unicom retained equipment, data-center space and network ties in the US despite FCC actions revoking their authority to provide certain telecom services from 2019-2022.
China Mobile International's network appeared in routes to Salt Typhoon-linked servers at least 192 times during Sept. 22-25, 2024.

The committee identified nearly 109,000 incidents from January 2018 through May 2025 of alleged unauthorized BGP hijacks by Chinese or Hong Kong-linked networks, over 4,200 involving China Mobile-controlled networks.
China Telecom Americas reported about a quarter of its U.S. transmission hardware was still made by Huawei, which the FCC has deemed a national security threat.

China Mobile purchased U.S. data center space and network connections on behalf of CloudRadium, a Hong Kong hosting provider linked to malicious cyber activity, via a four-year contract valued at $480,000.
